post_template.hook_style: Open with a direct, locally anchored question or bold statement tied to East Auckland autumn urgency or interest rate movement — confirmed high-relevance themes across all five April 2026 research briefs. Best-performing Facebook posts (engagement 3 at 08:00 on April 19 and engagement 2 at 10:00 on April 13) were both image posts, indicating the hook must work in tandem with a strong visual rather than as standalone text. Top-performing hook patterns drawn from research briefs and aligned with voice guide: 'Thinking of selling this autumn? Here is what most homeowners miss.' or 'The market just shifted — here is what it means for your home.' or 'Most buyers do not know this about East Auckland right now.' or 'Before you list your home, ask yourself these 3 questions.' or 'This is what a premium result actually looks like in 2026.' Hook must appear in the first line before any line break. Must include East Auckland geographic anchoring — generic national openers flagged across all five research briefs as a format to avoid. Interest rate cuts and autumn listing timing are the two highest-confidence hook themes for this period and must anchor at least two hooks per week across all platforms.
post_template.structure: hook → value or education point → local East Auckland relevance → soft CTA
post_template.best_performing_format: Low confidence — Facebook reach and impression data returned zero across all 14 posts analysed, indicating a likely API or data collection issue rather than true zero performance. The two highest raw engagement scores in the period were 3 and 2, both from image posts published at 08:00 and 10:00 respectively on April 19 and April 13, confirming image posts as the leading format by available engagement signal even within a low-data environment. All 4 archived local posts were text-only with zero image or video content, representing a critical and ongoing format gap that directly contradicts brand identity visual guidelines and all five research brief recommendations. Based on April 2026 research data across five separate briefs, image posts with lifestyle-driven visuals and education-focused captions are the recommended primary format. Short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format across multiple research briefs and must be introduced as a weekly priority on Instagram Reels and TikTok. Text-only posts are deprioritised to a maximum 25 percent of weekly output. Image-to-text ratio target is 3:1 minimum until a reliable engagement baseline is established over the next 30-day period.
retired_formats: Standalone text-only posts as the default or dominant weekly format — all 4 archived local posts in the period were text-only with no image or video content recorded; the two highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period were both image posts published at 08:00 and 10:00; research briefs consistently recommend image-led and short-form video formats over text-only across all five April 2026 briefs; text-only is reduced to a maximum supporting role at 25 percent of weekly output and should be reserved exclusively for high-value education angles such as interest rate commentary, buyer checklists, or market insight posts where data-led standalone copy adds clear value without requiring visual support

top_performing_types: listing — hero interior and exterior shots showcasing lifestyle, indoor-outdoor flow, and premium East Auckland homes; recommended as primary format based on brand identity guidelines and the two highest-engagement Facebook posts both being image posts at 08:00 and 10:00; low confidence due to zero reach and impression data in current period; must be published at confirmed peak hours of 08:00 or 10:00 to replicate the conditions of the top-performing posts

lifestyle — family living moments, warm autumn-toned interiors, soft natural light through windows, indoor-outdoor connection; seasonal alignment with Autumn 2026 context confirmed across all five research briefs; autumn lifestyle framing is the dominant seasonal content opportunity cited this period and should be the visual tone applied across all image post types through end of April into early May

sold — celebration moments, sold sticker overlays, happy client handovers at front door with genuine emotion; social proof format cited across three separate research briefs as a direct trust-building driver of seller enquiries; entirely absent from the current 4-post archive making it the single highest-priority image type to introduce immediately; at least one sold story image post per week is recommended as a non-negotiable content element

local_area — East Auckland streets, parks, school zones, suburban greenery, tree-lined streets, coastal lifestyle shots; suburb spotlight and school zone content noted across multiple research briefs as consistently building local authority and trust with family buyer audiences; currently absent from the archive and underrepresented relative to recommended content pillar weighting; aligns with autumn school-term family research cycle making it timely and high-relevance right now

agent_brand — Jinny interacting with clients at open homes, behind-the-scenes of listing process, professional yet warm and approachable moments; transparency and personal brand content cited in the April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions; absent from current archive and recommended for introduction to close the social proof and personality content gap
deprioritise_types: generic stock images with no local East Auckland relevance — flagged in brand identity avoid list and across multiple research briefs as undermining local authority positioning and failing to connect with the target East Auckland audience; all visuals must reflect recognisable East Auckland homes, streets, schools, or lifestyle contexts

text-only post cards or graphic tiles without supporting lifestyle or property photography — no performance data supports this format over image-led posts; conflicts with brand visual identity guidelines and all five research brief recommendations for 2026 real estate social content; use only as a secondary supporting format at maximum 25 percent of weekly output
image_strategy.overlay_style: Short punchy headline overlay in brand black (#000000) or brand white (#FFFFFF) placed on clean negative space areas of the image — maximum 2 to 6 words per overlay aligned with brand voice guide. Subtle brand red (#C8102E) used sparingly as an accent on key words, underlines, or thin divider elements only — never as a full background. Compositions must intentionally include negative space at the top or bottom third for overlay placement. Examples aligned to voice guide: 'Sell smarter.', 'This one won't last.', 'East Auckland living.', 'Buy with confidence.', 'Your next move starts here.', 'Don't overpay.' Overlay text must never cover the primary visual selling feature of the image. Font weight should be bold and legible at mobile screen sizes.

retired: No hashtags formally retired at this stage — low confidence period with only 4 archived posts and zero measurable reach or impression data returned from Facebook insights across all 14 posts analysed; insufficient data to confirm any tag as underperforming in reach or discovery terms; all previously active tags carried forward for continued monitoring; retirement decisions deferred to next 30-day review once reliable engagement and reach data is available to confirm which tags are generating discovery versus producing no traction across the East Auckland target audience

Trends and Short-form Content — short-form video under 30 seconds is flagged as the highest watch-through format in April 2026 across multiple research briefs; introducing at least one TikTok or Instagram Reel per week is the single highest-priority format gap to close given the current text-only archive; behind-the-scenes listing process content, open home walkthroughs, quick property tip videos, and one-thing-sellers-forget formats are the recommended entry formats for this pillar

Personal Brand and Trust — behind-the-scenes listing process content and transparency posts cited in the April 23 research brief as trust-building during active market conditions; sold celebration stories and client handover moments are entirely absent from the current 4-post archive and must be introduced immediately as a weekly priority to build social proof with potential sellers who are evaluating agents right now during the active autumn season

Listings and Success Stories — sold results and client success case studies cited across three of five research briefs as social proof drivers of seller enquiries; this format is entirely absent from the current archive and represents the most significant missed trust-conversion opportunity; at least one sold story or case study post per week is recommended immediately and should be maintained as a non-negotiable weekly content element until a visible social proof pattern is established on the profile
decrease_focus: Text-only standalone posts as primary content — all 4 archived posts were text-only with no image or video content recorded; the two highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period were both image posts, reinforcing the priority of visual formats; reduce text-only to a maximum 25 percent of weekly output and use only for high-value education angles such as interest rate commentary, buyer checklists, or market insights where standalone copy adds clear value without requiring visual support

Generic market commentary without local East Auckland context — flagged across all five research briefs as a content type to avoid; all market updates, rate commentary, and suburb insights must include East Auckland-specific or suburb-level framing to maintain local authority positioning and avoid being perceived as generic national content by the target East Auckland homeowner audience

optimal_times: 08:00 — highest single-post engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 3, image post, April 19); confirmed as a top-performing hour in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for morning-scroll educational content and listing reveals targeting commuters and early risers in East Auckland; image posts at this hour produced the strongest available engagement signal in the data period and should be prioritised for seller education and listing content

10:00 — second-highest engagement score in the Facebook insights period (engagement 2, image post, April 13); confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours; recommended for mid-morning market update and buyer guidance content when the East Auckland audience is actively browsing on mobile during mid-morning routines; image format confirmed as the top format at this hour

21:00 — confirmed in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and appearing in 2 of the top 5 Facebook insight posts with engagement scores of 1 each; closely aligned with the consistent 20:00 posting pattern across all 4 archived local posts; recommended as the primary evening window targeting homeowners in a relaxed end-of-day planning mindset; best suited for seller education, community content, and interest rate commentary when audiences are in a reflective decision-making state

20:00 — most common posting hour across all 4 archived local posts; retained as a secondary evening fallback window closely aligned with the 21:00 insights peak; use when 21:00 scheduling is unavailable or when content is time-sensitive on a given day; avoid making this the only posting window as the previous strategy did — split scheduling across morning and evening windows is now the recommended approach
best_days: Tuesday through Thursday recommended as primary posting days for seller education, market update, and buyer guidance content based on general real estate social media best practices — low confidence due to insufficient day-level performance data in the current Facebook insights period; reassess when day-level engagement data becomes available in the next 30-day review cycle

Saturday morning at 08:00 to 10:00 recommended for listing reveals, open home announcements, and sold result posts to align with weekend buyer browsing and open home activity patterns in East Auckland — supported by 08:00 and 10:00 confirmed as top-performing hours in facebook_insights.best_posting_hours and general real estate audience behaviour on weekends

Sunday evening at 20:00 to 21:00 recommended for seller education and week-ahead market content targeting East Auckland homeowners in a relaxed end-of-weekend planning mindset — supported by the 21:00 performance signal from Facebook insights and the consistent 20:00 archive posting pattern; autumn urgency and interest rate hooks are the recommended content themes for this slot
posting_schedule.image_to_text_ratio: 3:1 — minimum three image or video posts for every one text-only post per week; the current archive is 0:4 in favour of text which is the inverse of recommended best practice per brand identity visual guidelines and all five research briefs; the two highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period were both image posts confirming visual formats outperform text even in a low-data environment; this ratio shift is the most urgent tactical change required this period and must be implemented and maintained from the current week forward

Image posts outperform text posts in all available engagement data — the two highest-engagement posts in the period (scores of 3 and 2) were both image posts; the lowest-engagement posts scoring 1 each included text-only entries; while the sample size is too small for statistical confidence, this directional signal is consistent with all five research briefs recommending image-led formats over text-only for 2026 real estate social content and must inform immediate format decisions

All 4 archived local posts were text-only with no image or video content — this is a critical and ongoing content gap directly contradicting the brand image strategy, brand identity visual guidelines, and the format recommendations of all five research briefs; the absence of sold stories, suburb spotlights, agent brand moments, and short-form video from the archive represents the most significant strategic gap to close in the next 30 days and has not improved from the previous strategy period

Interest rate cuts are confirmed as a high-relevance topic across all five research briefs and represent a dual-audience opportunity — addressing buyer confidence and seller urgency in a single content angle; this is the strongest single evergreen hook available for the current period and should anchor at least one post per week across Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok with East Auckland-specific framing applied in every case

School zone property demand and East Auckland suburb spotlights are consistently cited across multiple research briefs as high-performing local authority content for family buyer audiences; this content type is currently absent from the archive, aligns with the autumn school-term family research cycle, and represents a timely and differentiated opportunity to build local expert positioning distinct from generic agent content

Morning posting at 08:00 and 10:00 is confirmed as the highest-engagement window from Facebook insights data — the two highest-engagement posts in the period were published at these hours; the previous strategy defaulted entirely to 20:00 evening posting across all 4 archived posts with no morning scheduling tested; a split schedule combining confirmed morning peaks and evening windows is now recommended to maximise reach across different audience browsing patterns in East Auckland

reasoning.what_worked: The two highest-engagement posts in the Facebook insights period (engagement scores of 3 and 2) were both image posts published at 08:00 and 10:00 respectively on April 19 and April 13 — confirming that image format combined with morning scheduling produces the strongest available engagement signal in this period even within a low-confidence data environment. Evening posting at 21:00 appeared in 2 of the top 5 posts with engagement scores of 1 each, consistent with the existing 20:00 archive posting pattern and confirming the evening window as a reliable secondary slot. Core brand hashtags were applied consistently across all 4 archived posts maintaining brand discoverability continuity. The autumn urgency and interest rate angles recommended across all five research briefs remain the strongest available thematic hooks for the current period and continue to represent high-confidence content opportunities that are not yet fully utilised in the archive.
reasoning.what_didnt: All 4 archived local posts were text-only with no image or video content for the second consecutive strategy period, directly contradicting brand visual identity guidelines, the image-led engagement signal from Facebook insights, and the format recommendations of all five research briefs. The 0:4 image-to-text ratio in the archive remains the inverse of the 3:1 ratio recommended by brand identity and research guidance. No personal brand content, sold stories, suburb spotlights, open home content, or short-form video appeared in the archive across the full 30-day period — all of which are cited as high-performing trust-building and engagement formats across multiple research briefs. Posting was uniformly at 20:00 across all 4 archived posts with no morning scheduling tested despite 08:00 and 10:00 being confirmed as the top-performing hours in Facebook insights data. The failure to shift format mix in the previous period means the most urgent tactical recommendation remains unchanged and must be actioned immediately.
reasoning.main_recommendation: Immediately shift the weekly content mix to a minimum 3:1 image-to-text ratio by introducing lifestyle property photography, sold success story images, and at least one short-form video per week on Instagram Reels or TikTok — this is the most urgent and overdue tactical change given the text-only archive across two consecutive strategy periods. Prioritise autumn seller education content and interest rate hooks with local East Auckland framing published at 08:00 or 10:00 for morning reach and 21:00 for evening engagement based on confirmed Facebook insights best posting hours. Add one sold success story or suburb spotlight image post every week as a non-negotiable content element to begin building social proof and local authority — both formats are entirely absent from the current archive and cited across multiple research briefs as the highest-trust content types for converting seller enquiries in the East Auckland market.
